title: The acceptance-length question: what should M3 measure, and how deep should the chain draft?

justifications.a: First measure and ensure we improve and dont regress. even single stream/session must not regress

justifications.b: as long as it benefits to have it and we can make sure it makes things better rather than worse

spec.title: The acceptance-length question: what should M3 measure, and how deep should the chain draft?
spec.intro:
**What this decides.** Three linked things: whether the MTP draft floor `--spec-min-p` moves off its standing 0.7, what the six-metric law's M3 should actually measure, and which of six unused levers the engine's own code and the field's practice put on the board.

**Why now.** Lowering the floor to 0.5 or 0.35 measured **+8–11% throughput** with **tokens per verify window rising 2.2 → 2.5**, and the acceptance **rate** falling 91% → 87%. Your law protects the rate, so it vetoes the change. The push sent me to research, not intuition: **eighteen comparables** were studied from primary sources and written to `.docs/research/` with a digest at `.docs/digest/speculative-draft-yield-and-acceptance-metrics.md`.

**What the research found, in one line.** *No surveyed system treats acceptance rate as its objective or as a protected metric.* The field's headline is **acceptance length** — tokens per forward pass — which is exactly our tokens/window, and it **rises** in our measurement. vLLM names it `mean_acceptance_length`; SGLang's is `spec_accept_length`; TensorRT-LLM computes `acceptance_length` as output tokens per decoding iteration; MLC-LLM publishes cumulative `accept_len`; EAGLE's τ is "the average number of tokens accepted per forward pass". EAGLE-2 states outright: *"Why is acceptance rate not included? The acceptance rate only reflects the performance of the draft model."* HuggingFace TGI ships speculation with **no acceptance metric at all**. And vLLM's own tuning PR measured the case that settles it: on RTX 4050 + Qwen2.5-7B, fixed K=5 gave 75.2 tok/s at length 1.88, adaptive K gave **75.9** at 1.86, and oracle K=12 gave **60.8 tok/s at length 2.27 — the highest acceptance length, 19% slower**.

**Where our own floor sits.** Ours is the highest fixed floor in the survey: llama.cpp ships its probability floor **disabled by default** (0.00) and its community landed at 0.6–0.8, one report finding 0.70 *17–21% slower* on reasoning text; ExLlamaV2 hard-codes 0.25; Medusa and Hydra sweep ε over 0.05–0.25; vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, SGLang and TGI have no such floor at all. At 0.7 our chain tests only ~1.4 drafts per window — **the floor, not the draft head, is what limits our depth.**

**What else the research turned up that we already own but do not use.** Our engine ships a `DraftPolicy` that learns measured tokens-per-window and milliseconds-per-window for each window size and picks by **expected committed tokens per millisecond** — the same objective as vLLM's goodput rule and SGLang's adaptive controller — but it only chooses MTP *versus lookup*, never the MTP depth. We have a per-position instrument (`STRATA_SPEC_DEPTH=1`) that has never been armed. Our concurrent path runs **entirely draftless** ("slot drafts accepted 0 of 0") while every surveyed engine keys draft depth to batch size. And our typical-acceptance rescue is a bare constant where Medusa uses an entropy-scaled threshold.

**What happens with your answers.** The first answer sets the floor decision and opens its own branch; the later questions set what M3 measures, what instrumentation gets armed, and where the next session works. If a config change is approved it is one line in `strata-iq3_s.json`, gated and revertible. **Nothing is adopted until you answer. About four minutes.**

gate_choice.prompt: The MTP draft floor `--spec-min-p` stands at 0.7: the verify window stops extending when the next draft's probability falls below it. Lowering it measured +8-11% throughput with tokens/window rising 2.2 -> 2.5, while the acceptance rate fell 91% -> 87%, and the research found no comparable that protects that rate or uses it as its objective. What should the standing recipe carry?

options.label: Keep 0.7 - no metric moves
options.description: Choosing this leaves the standing recipe exactly as it is: the rate stays above 90% and no metric moves in either direction.
options.insight:
- **Measured in the same window:** 0.7 gives 159.8 and 146.9 t/s at tokens/window 2.18 and 2.09, with the rate at 90.1% and 90.9% (campaign/results/minp-quiet-1.txt).
- **What it costs:** the chain tests only ~1.4 drafts per window (927 drafts over ~680 windows), so the floor and not the draft head is what limits our depth.
- **Where it sits in the field:** ours is the highest fixed floor in the survey - llama.cpp ships its floor disabled by default and its community landed at 0.6-0.8, ExLlamaV2 hard-codes 0.25, Medusa and Hydra sweep 0.05-0.25, and vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, SGLang and TGI have no floor at all.
- **Breaks when:** a workload's drafting is already near-certain, where the floor buys nothing and the window still pays for every offered draft.

options.label: Adopt 0.5 - the best measured throughput
options.description: Choosing this sets the floor to 0.5 in the standing config, taking throughput up 8-11% and the acceptance rate down about 4.5 points.
options.insight:
- **Measured, interleaved, same window:** 151.9 vs 136.4 t/s (+11.4%) and 145.4 vs 135.1 (+7.6%), with tokens/window 2.63 and 2.49 against 2.17 and 2.25.
- **The metric that rises is the field's headline:** our tokens/window is vLLM's `mean_acceptance_length`, SGLang's `spec_accept_length` and TensorRT-LLM's `acceptance_length`; all three treat it as the objective and the rate as a diagnostic.
- **Comparable precedent for exactly this trade:** llama.cpp discussion #25198 accepts acceptance 67.8% -> 55.7% for +20.4% throughput with the floor at 0.8 and n-max 16, and one report there has 0.70 as 17-21% slower on reasoning text.
- **Breaks when:** the window grows faster than the tokens it banks - ReDrafter's beam width 4 keeps 2.44 tokens/step but collapses speedup from 1.52x to 0.75x, which is the shape our own 0.0-floor arm showed (3.97 tokens/window at 16.57 ms, 152.8 t/s).

options.label: Adopt 0.35 - the deepest chain
options.description: Choosing this sets the floor to 0.35, drafting deepest: the largest tokens-per-window measured, 2.80-2.96, at the same acceptance-rate cost as 0.5.
options.insight:
- **Measured:** won 5 of 6 interleaved comparisons across both runs, one tie, none lost; 166.8 vs 159.8 and 163.1 vs 146.9 t/s.
- **The strongest single signal:** tokens/window came out 2.80, 2.96, 2.86, 2.86 against 2.18, 2.09, 2.33, 2.37 for 0.7 - non-overlapping ranges.
- **What it costs that 0.5 does not:** the window grows to 14.8-15.8 ms against 13.0 ms, so more of the gain is spent buying itself; TensorRT-LLM caps our exact model (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next) at `max_draft_len` 3, and our `--spec 4` already runs a 6-token window.
- **Here now:** the lowest acceptance rate measured tonight, 84.8-86.6%.

options.label: Gate it first: MMLU-Pro and mimic, then decide
options.description: Choosing this leaves the config alone while the two graded suites are measured in the same window, and the adoption waits for those numbers.
options.insight:
- **Why the gate is real here:** the floor is not the distribution-bending kind of acceptance - every offered draft is still verified exactly against the target - but Medusa's *typical* acceptance is explicitly not lossless ("typically unnecessary to match the distribution of the original model"), and our recipe arms that rescue at 0.2.
- **The measured size of the risk:** TensorRT-LLM reports our exact model at GSM8K 95.11 with MTP3 against 95.72 in BF16 - a small, real, depth-related gap.
- **Cost:** one boot plus two graded suites, both needing the lane exclusively.
- **Here now:** MMLU-Pro stands at 95.7 from 16:48 today and mimic has not been re-run since the T1e boot.

options.label: Explore below 0.5 with per-position data armed
options.description: Choosing this measures the floor further down - 0.5, 0.35, 0.25, 0.1 - with the engine's per-depth counter switched on so the curve is visible, before any value is adopted.
options.insight:
- **Why below 0.5 is not exotic:** Medusa and Hydra sweep their threshold over 0.05-0.25, an order of magnitude below our floor, and llama.cpp's floor is disabled by default.
- **What the per-position view buys:** every surveyed engine reports acceptance per draft position (vLLM `..._num_accepted_tokens_per_pos{position}`, MLC `accept_rate{step=i}`, EAGLE-3's 0-alpha through 4-alpha) because a blended ratio cannot say *where* a chain dies - EAGLE-3 used that resolution to find a collapsing second-position rate masked by a rising first.
- **We already own the instrument and have never run it:** `STRATA_SPEC_DEPTH=1` prints accepted/tested for the first five depths (src/program/generate.cpp:12659).
- **Cost:** one boot and a sweep that the per-request tuning key makes possible in a single window, about two minutes per pass.

options.label: Replace the fixed floor with policy-driven depth
options.description: Choosing this makes the chain length a runtime decision from the engine's own measured cost tables instead of a constant, so depth adapts to the content and the machine.
options.insight:
- **The engine already computes the right objective:** `DraftPolicy` (include/strata/spec/draft_policy.hpp) learns EMA tokens-per-window and milliseconds-per-window for each window size and picks by expected committed tokens per millisecond - the same objective as vLLM's goodput rule and SGLang's adaptive controller.
- **What it does not do:** `choose()` clamps the window to the MTP's own size (`p.t = clamp(t_mtp, 1, max_t_)`), so it only ever switches to a lookup window; the depth decision is still the fixed floor.
- **The field's precedent:** SGLang's `--speculative-adaptive` steers depth from an EMA of accept length with hysteresis; vLLM and TensorRT-LLM key depth to batch size instead; every mechanism found optimises throughput or latency and none optimises the acceptance rate.
- **Honest cost:** this is engine work with a test to write, not a config line, and its wins are unmeasured until the tables are wired to the depth decision.

status_quo_next.prompt: The floor stays at 0.7. Where should the effort go instead?

options.label: The miss path - expert cache hit rate
options.description: Choosing this attacks the term that dominates a degraded window: the CPU side is missed experts times about 85 microseconds each.
options.insight:
- **Measured law:** the CPU term equals misses per layer-window times 48 layers times ~85 us, and the hit rate ranged 79.5-99.2% on a single boot.
- **The prize:** the real-workload class at tokens/window 3.96 read 34.82 ms at an 88.9% hit rate; at the healthy 97.9% the same request computes to ~15 ms, about 264 t/s - above the 232 bar.
- **Here now:** the PCIe split that would move those misses is measured and worth only +-4%, so the lever is the residency decision, not the split.

options.label: The R17 draft head - raise acceptance itself
options.description: Choosing this works the trained head so each draft is likelier to be right, which raises throughput with no acceptance-rate cost at all.
options.insight:
- **Where it stands:** the chain is validated at 85.4% stock round-trip and the distilled checkpoint reached 57.4% against the stock 85.4%, blocked on mixed-KV conditioning.
- **Why the field says train it:** FastMTP measured a reused head at 70%/11%/2% across depths 1/2/3 and 81%/56%/36% after multi-step fine-tuning - the later positions are designed, not merely reused.
- **Cost:** hours of training runs, and the lane only at the final gates.

options.label: Instrumentation first: per-position and the batch path
options.description: Choosing this spends the session on the two measurement gaps the research exposed before touching any value.
options.insight:
- **Gap one:** we have no per-position acceptance, while four surveyed systems publish it; `STRATA_SPEC_DEPTH=1` exists and has never been armed.
- **Gap two:** our concurrent path runs entirely draftless ("slot drafts accepted 0 of 0") while vLLM, TensorRT-LLM and MLC-LLM all key draft depth to batch size.
- **Why it pays:** these make every later adoption decidable instead of arguable, which is the standard the push asked for.

options.label: Nothing further on this axis - the law stands as written
options.description: Choosing this accepts 0.7 as correct and stops spending sessions on the draft-yield axis.
options.insight:
- **Consequence:** the standing config stays below the frontier measured tonight (tokens/window 2.5-2.9), and the 232 bar keeps its full 8-11% deficit on this axis.
- **Breaks when:** the next session re-derives the same trade and reaches the same veto, which is what the research was meant to prevent.

options.label: Re-measure the trade on more content classes first
options.description: Choosing this repeats the interleaved comparison across the four-class sweep so the decision rests on more than one content shape.
options.insight:
- **Why it is defensible:** tonight's floor comparison ran on two content shapes; the four-class sweep showed tokens/window ranging 2.5-4.0 across classes at one floor setting.
- **Cost:** minutes, using the same single-boot instrument.
- **Breaks when:** the classes differ so much that a single standing value cannot serve them - which is the argument for policy-driven depth rather than any constant.

quality_gate.prompt: Before the floor change is committed, should MMLU-Pro and mimic be measured in the same window?

options.label: Yes - both, before the commit
options.description: Choosing this runs both graded suites first and holds the config until they come back at or above their standing values.
options.insight:
- **What it buys:** the only evidence that can refute the invariance argument, on the two metrics that measure the model rather than the scheduler.
- **Why the argument is not self-evidently safe:** our recipe arms a typical-acceptance rescue at 0.2, and Medusa states that scheme is deliberately not distribution-matching.
- **Cost:** one boot and two suites on a lane verified quiet.

options.label: Yes - MMLU-Pro only
options.description: Choosing this runs the graded knowledge suite alone and accepts mimic on the invariance argument.
options.insight:
- **Why it is reasonable:** MMLU-Pro is the metric this campaign has seen bend (the batch-rescue arm took it 95.7 -> 91.4-92.9), while mimic has not moved on a scheduling arm.
- **Cost:** about half the gating time.
- **Breaks when:** a change shows up as compliance or formatting rather than knowledge, which is what mimic exists to catch.

options.label: No - commit now and re-measure after
options.description: Choosing this adopts on the measured throughput, the invariance argument and the field's practice, and schedules the suites afterwards.
options.insight:
- **What it rests on:** a rejected draft never reaches the output and an accepted one is the token the target would itself have sampled, so the emitted sequence is unchanged by the floor.
- **The field's corroboration:** no surveyed engine defends an acceptance rate, and the closest shipped relative (TensorRT-LLM `relaxed_topk`/`relaxed_delta`) trades acceptance for speed at a declared cost.
- **Cheapest insurance:** the change is one config line to revert.

options.label: No - and mark the adoption provisional for one session
options.description: Choosing this adopts now and records the change as provisional until one session of real use confirms it.
options.insight:
- **Pattern:** the completion criteria already require the bar to hold across three stable consecutive sessions, so a provisional flag matches the standing law rather than weakening it.
- **Breaks when:** the flag outlives the session it was meant to cover, which is why it carries an expiry.

options.label: Yes - both, plus the full six-metric probe
options.description: Choosing this runs the graded suites and re-anchors all six metrics in one window before the commit.
options.insight:
- **What it buys:** a complete baseline row for the chart, which is what the trend law asks each session to carry.
- **Cost:** the longest gate on the menu, and the concurrency probes need the lane to themselves.
- **Here now:** tonight's window already reads 157.8 t/s at 13.29 ms and a 110.7 pair aggregate, so the baseline half is partly paid for.

gate_value.prompt: The gate is to be run before the decision. Which floor value should it be run on?

options.description: Choosing this gates the value with the best measured throughput tonight.
options.insight:
- **Measured:** +11.4% and +7.6% in two interleaved passes at a 4.3-point rate cost.
- **Why first:** it is the middle of the measured frontier, so a pass implies the more aggressive value is worth testing next.
- **Here now:** nothing adopted, so this would be the first M4/M5 measurement against the knob.

options.description: Choosing this gates the deepest chain measured.
options.insight:
- **Measured:** tokens/window 2.76-2.96 against 2.09-2.41 for the standing value, winning or tying every interleaved comparison.
- **Why gate this one:** it is the largest effect, so a pass here covers the whole range below 0.7.
- **Cost:** the lowest rate measured tonight, 84.8%.

options.label: Both 0.5 and 0.35
options.description: Choosing this gates both candidates so the decision can discriminate on quality as well as speed.
options.insight:
- **What it buys:** the two values measured within 3% of each other on throughput, so quality becomes the only remaining discriminator.
- **Cost:** two graded suites per value, on a quiet lane.

options.label: 0.6 - a smaller step
options.description: Choosing this gates a value between the standing 0.7 and the measured candidates, taking a smaller share of the effect.
options.insight:
- **Why it exists:** if the rate cost is linear in chain depth, half the step takes half the cost.
- **Unmeasured:** 0.6 has not been run, so its tokens/window and rate are unknown; the sweep measures it in about thirty seconds.
- **Breaks when:** the floor is not binding for that content, in which case 0.6 and 0.7 measure the same.

options.label: Let tools/calibrate.py pick it on the live engine
options.description: Choosing this runs the engine's own calibration tool, which sweeps the floor and the PCIe split on a running engine and reports the best pair.
options.insight:
- **What it is:** `tools/calibrate.py` sweeps `SPEC_MIN_PS = (0.3, 0.5, 0.7)` and `PCIE_FRACS` over seven values on a live engine, using the per-request tuning keys, and reports its pick.
- **What tonight adds:** the split is worth +-4% and the floor 8-11%, so the two axes are not equally valuable; the tool's grid also stops at 0.3 while tonight's frontier sat between 0.35 and 0.5.
- **Here now:** the standing config bypasses the tool entirely - `--pcie-frac 0.35` is explicit, which also stops the link probe from running.

m3_definition.prompt: The research found no surveyed engine that treats acceptance rate as its objective or as a non-regression metric, while the quantity that rises in our measurement - tokens per verify window - is their shared headline. What should M3 measure from now on?

options.label: Acceptance rate, exactly as today
options.description: Choosing this keeps M3 as accepted drafts divided by tested drafts, unchanged.
options.insight:
- **What it measures:** how often an offered draft is right, over a chain whose length the floor itself decides, so the denominator moves whenever depth moves.
- **Consequence, measured:** every floor-lowering change reads as an M3 regression even when both throughput and tokens-per-window rise.
- **Why that is not comparable across settings:** for a fixed depth-4 chain the expected banked tokens are alpha+alpha^2+alpha^3+alpha^4, about 3.18 at alpha 0.91 and 2.86 at 0.87 - a fall - while we measured a rise, so our logged rate is not the chain's alpha.

options.label: Tokens per verify window - the field's acceptance length
options.description: Choosing this makes M3 the tokens the engine banks per verify window, the quantity every surveyed engine leads with.
options.insight:
- **The field's own names for it:** vLLM `mean_acceptance_length` (1 + accepted drafts / steps, range 1.0 to k+1), SGLang `spec_accept_length`, TensorRT-LLM `acceptance_length` (output tokens per decoding iteration), MLC-LLM cumulative `accept_len`, EAGLE's tau = tokens accepted per forward pass.
- **What it does under this change:** it RISES, 2.2 -> 2.5, so the trade stops being a trade on this axis.
- **Why it resists gaming:** both the chain depth and the per-draft hit rate feed into it, unlike either alone.
- **Must be recorded as a metric change** with a dated entry, not as a win.

options.label: Both, printed side by side in every report
options.description: Choosing this keeps the rate and adds tokens per window, requiring both numbers wherever M3 is quoted.
options.insight:
- **What the field does:** the systems that compute both publish them together, and ExLlamaV2 names them separately as `accuracy` (the rate) and `efficiency` (the length).
- **Cost:** zero - the engine already prints `T`, `tokens/window` and `drafts accepted N of M` in the same request's lines.
- **Breaks when:** a reader picks whichever number looks better, which is why the report must state which one is the objective.

options.label: Rate at a fixed reference depth only
options.description: Choosing this keeps the rate but measures it at one declared chain depth, so it stays comparable across settings.
options.insight:
- **Why it fixes the comparability problem:** the denominator stops moving with the floor.
- **What it costs:** it is a metric the engine does not currently produce - the per-depth counters exist (`STRATA_SPEC_DEPTH=1`) but the request-level rate is blended.
- **Breaks when:** the operating depth is itself the thing being changed, which is exactly this decision.

options.label: Accepted tokens per millisecond - the objective the engine already uses
options.description: Choosing this makes M3 the rate of banked tokens per unit time, which is what the engine's own draft policy optimises.
options.insight:
- **Already the engine's stated objective:** `DraftPolicy` compares expected committed tokens per millisecond, and vLLM's adaptive-verification rule maximises expected accepted tokens per unit step time.
- **The counter-example that proves the point:** on RTX 4050 + Qwen2.5-7B the highest acceptance length (2.27) ran 19% slower than a lower one (1.86), so length alone is not sufficient either.
- **Here now:** milliseconds-per-window is already the campaign's degradation signal, so the pairing is one division away.

options.label: Drop M3 and run five metrics
options.description: Choosing this removes acceptance from the scoreboard entirely.
options.insight:
- **The case:** one production engine (HuggingFace TGI) ships speculation with no acceptance metric at all, and EAGLE-2 declines to publish the rate with a stated reason.
- **The case against:** the metric exists because a broken drafter once looked fast while accepting almost nothing, and removing it removes the only guard on draft quality.
- **Not recommended** on the evidence here.

m3_reporting.prompt: Where should the new M3 reading live so it is actually carried?

options.label: Amend the law in AGENTS.md
options.description: Choosing this rewrites the six-metric clause so M3 names the new quantity, with the change dated.
options.insight:
- **Why the law and not just the chart:** the veto came from the law's wording, so leaving the wording leaves the veto.
- **What the amendment must carry:** the old and new definitions, the date, and a note that the rate remains reported as a diagnostic.

options.label: Add the columns to PERF-CHART.md
options.description: Choosing this makes the standing chart carry the rate, tokens per window and accepted tokens per millisecond as separate columns.
options.insight:
- **Why the chart:** every adoption is gated against it, so it is where a regression would actually be seen.
- **Here now:** the chart's M3 row reads a single acceptance percentage with no length beside it.

options.label: Make probe-lane print all three
options.description: Choosing this changes the standard probe's output so every future run carries the three numbers without anyone remembering to.
options.insight:
- **Why the instrument:** the campaign's rule is that a number which is not printed does not exist.
- **Cost:** a small edit to campaign/probe-lane.ps1, which already parses the engine's acceptance line.

options.label: Publish the per-position vector too
options.description: Choosing this adds the acceptance-by-depth breakdown to the standard report.
options.insight:
- **The field precedent:** vLLM, llama.cpp, MLC-LLM and EAGLE-3 all publish acceptance per position, and EAGLE-3 used exactly that resolution to find its own bottleneck.
- **We own the instrument:** `STRATA_SPEC_DEPTH=1` prints accepted/tested for five depths and has never been armed.

options.label: Record it in SVG-CUSTOM.md only
options.description: Choosing this writes the new reading into the flight log and leaves the law and the instruments untouched.
options.insight:
- **Cost:** the next session must read the entry to know the rule, whereas the law is read first by construction.
- **Breaks when:** a later session quotes the old M3 row of the chart without the entry.

deep_sweep.prompt: The floor should be explored further down. Which sweep, and with what armed?

options.label: 0.5, 0.35, 0.25, 0.1 with per-position armed
options.description: Choosing this sweeps four floors in one boot with the per-depth counter on, so the whole curve and where it dies are visible together.
options.insight:
- **Why the range:** Medusa and Hydra sweep their threshold over 0.05-0.25, so 0.1 is inside published practice, and llama.cpp ships its floor disabled.
- **Why per-position:** it is the only resolution that says whether a lower floor rescues position 1 or buys position 4, and the engines that report it did so to find exactly that.
- **Cost:** two passes over four arms in one boot, about four minutes.

options.label: 0.5 against 0.35 only
options.description: Choosing this repeats tonight's two-arm comparison with more passes instead of widening the range.
options.insight:
- **Why it is the conservative choice:** both values are already measured, so more passes tighten the estimate rather than opening a new axis.
- **What it will not answer:** whether the curve keeps paying below 0.35, which is what the field's much lower thresholds suggest.

options.label: Sweep with the acceptance-length inversion as the target
options.description: Choosing this calibrates the floor by choosing the tokens-per-window to aim at and deriving what floor implies it.
options.insight:
- **The instrument exists in the field:** vLLM's `_acceptance_length_to_rates(length, n)` converts a target mean acceptance length into per-position rates via a minimum-variance schedule - the exact inverse of a probability floor.
- **Why it fits us:** it turns the floor from a guess into the solution of a stated objective, and the objective is the metric the research says matters.
- **Cost:** we would implement the inversion; the engine has the per-depth counters to fit it against.

options.label: Sweep across all four content classes, not one
options.description: Choosing this repeats the floor sweep on the four-class workload sweep so the value is not fitted to one content shape.
options.insight:
- **Why:** tokens/window ranged 2.5-4.0 across classes at a single floor, so the best floor may differ by content - which is also the argument for policy-driven depth.
- **Cost:** four times the requests, still in one boot.

options.label: Do not sweep further - 0.5 is the operating point
options.description: Choosing this stops the floor exploration at the best measured value and moves the effort elsewhere.
options.insight:
- **The argument:** ReDrafter's beam width 4 kept its tokens per step but collapsed speedup to 0.75x, so depth past the operating point is paid in wall clock.
- **The counter-argument:** our own 0.0-floor arm still gained on 3.97 tokens per window, so we have not yet found the turning point.

depth_policy.prompt: The chain length should become a runtime decision. What should the policy own?

options.label: The MTP depth only - the smallest real change
options.description: Choosing this wires the policy's existing cost tables to the MTP window size and leaves everything else alone.
options.insight:
- **What it uses:** `mtp_tok_[t]` and `cost_[t]`, the EMAs the policy already maintains for each window size, scored as tokens per millisecond.
- **Why it is small:** `choose()` already returns a window size; today it merely clamps it to the MTP's own, so the seam exists.
- **Breaks when:** the tables are cold at boot, which the policy already handles with scaled priors and probe rounds for unseen sizes.

options.label: Depth plus the lookup chain
options.description: Choosing this lets one policy choose both the MTP window and any chained lookup drafts that continue it.
options.insight:
- **What already exists:** `chain(t_mtp, p_mtp, k_avail, match)` picks how many lookup tokens to append by expected tokens per millisecond, but it is gated behind `--lookup-chain`, which is off by default.
- **The measured caution:** the one arm that tried `--lookup-chain 4 --suffix-draft 8` lost on all four classes, though it was compared across boots.
- **Why they belong together:** the header notes a long lookup window costs much more to verify than the MTP's usual 3-4 tokens, so the two decisions price each other.

options.label: Depth, margin and exploration
options.description: Choosing this also tunes the margin the policy requires to switch strategy and keeps its probe behaviour for unmeasured sizes.
options.insight:
- **What exists:** a `margin` parameter (default 0.03) and a probe rule that tries an unmeasured size when the lookup rate is at least 0.85.
- **Why it matters:** the margin decides how eagerly the engine leaves a known-good strategy, which is the same hysteresis SGLang's adaptive controller implements.

options.label: Full runtime autotuning, including batch-keyed depth
options.description: Choosing this makes the policy own depth per batch shape and content, with the config values becoming starting points only.
options.insight:
- **The field's practice:** vLLM keys depth to batch size (`num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size`), TensorRT-LLM uses `draft_len_schedule = {100: 4, 200: 3, 300: 2}`, MLC-LLM a fixed 4/3/2/0 table - all by batch size, none by drafter confidence.
- **Why it would pay here:** our concurrent path currently drafts nothing at all, so a batch-keyed rule is where that lane's unused speculation lives.
- **Cost:** the largest change on the menu, and it needs the batch path's draft staging to work first.

options.label: Nothing - use the policy as a diagnostic only
options.description: Choosing this reads the policy's learned tables to inform the config and changes no behaviour.
options.insight:
- **Why it is a real option:** the tables are the engine's own measurement of what each window size costs, which is better evidence than a config sweep across boots.
- **Cost:** nothing changes at runtime, so the frontier stays unexploited until a human edits the config.

options.label: Implement the field's goodput cost model first
options.description: Choosing this writes the explicit cost model the field uses - expected accepted tokens per unit step time - before wiring any behaviour to it.
options.insight:
- **What it is:** vLLM's adaptive rule and its PR #44336 budget rule maximise expected accepted tokens per unit step time, and SGLang steers on an accept-length EMA with batch-tier ceilings.
- **Why write it down first:** our policy's objective is already this, but its cost model is an EMA of round times rather than the field's explicit draft-cost plus verify-cost form, and an explicit model is testable.
- **Cost:** design plus a unit test, then the wiring.

policy_scope.prompt: Which signals should the depth decision read?

options.label: Measured round cost and banked tokens, as today
options.description: Choosing this keeps the policy on the two EMAs it already trusts: milliseconds per window and tokens committed per window.
options.insight:
- **Why it is enough to start:** it is measured on this machine, needs no model, and already adapts to context length.
- **Breaks when:** a window size has not been tried, which the policy covers with scaled priors and probe rounds.

options.label: Per-position acceptance
options.description: Choosing this feeds the acceptance rate at each draft position into the decision, so depth follows where the chain actually dies.
options.insight:
- **The field's resolution:** EAGLE-3 reports 0-alpha through 4-alpha per position and used that to find a collapsing second position masked by a rising first; vLLM, llama.cpp and MLC all publish per-position counters.
- **What we have:** `STRATA_SPEC_DEPTH=1` prints accepted/tested for five depths and has never been armed.
- **Why it could beat a scalar:** a blended rate cannot say whether position 2 or position 4 is the one failing.

options.label: Batch size and concurrency
options.description: Choosing this makes the batch shape a first-class input, since every surveyed engine keys depth to it.
options.insight:
- **The field's mechanism:** vLLM `num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size`, TensorRT-LLM `draft_len_schedule`, MLC-LLM's 4/3/2/0 table - three independent engines, one signal.
- **What it exposes here:** our pair path runs draftless ("slot drafts accepted 0 of 0"), so depth by batch is currently zero for every concurrent request.

options.label: Distribution entropy, Medusa's co-threshold
options.description: Choosing this scales the acceptance threshold by how flat the model's distribution is, instead of holding a constant.
options.insight:
- **The mechanism:** Medusa accepts when the draft is within `min(epsilon, delta * exp(-H(p)))` of the target's top choice, so acceptance widens automatically when the distribution is flat.
- **Why it fits us:** our rescue is a bare constant (`STRATA_TYPICAL_ACCEPT=0.2`) where the field's thresholds are entropy-scaled and swept over 0.05-0.25.
- **Caveat:** this family is deliberately not distribution-matching, so it is a quality knob and belongs behind the graded suites.

options.label: All four
options.description: Choosing this builds the decision on cost, per-position acceptance, batch shape and entropy together.
options.insight:
- **Why it is coherent:** they are the four inputs the surveyed systems use between them, and none is redundant - cost prices a window, position says where it fails, batch says how many rows ride along, entropy says how much confidence to demand.
- **Cost:** the most test surface, and each input needs a unit test to be trusted.

per_position_instrument.prompt: Every surveyed engine reports acceptance per draft position; we have an instrument for it that has never been armed. What should be done?

options.label: Arm STRATA_SPEC_DEPTH=1 at both floors in one window
options.description: Choosing this boots once with the per-depth counter on and reads where each floor's chain dies, before any value is adopted.
options.insight:
- **What it prints:** accepted/tested for the first five depths (src/program/generate.cpp:12659-12663) - the exact shape DeepSeek reports as 85-90% at depth 1 and FastMTP as 70%/11%/2% with a reused head.
- **Why it settles the argument:** it distinguishes 'the lower floor rescued position 1' from 'it bought position 4', which the blended rate cannot.
- **Cost:** one boot and two probe requests.

options.label: Add a persistent per-position counter to the log
options.description: Choosing this makes the per-position vector a permanent part of the request line rather than a diagnostic boot.
options.insight:
- **The field's form:** vLLM `vllm:spec_decode_num_accepted_tokens_per_pos{position}`, llama.cpp `..._per_pos_total{position}`, MLC `accept_rate{step=i}`.
- **Why permanent:** the campaign's rule is that an unprinted number does not exist, and tonight's 91% -> 87% question was unanswerable without it.

options.label: Calibrate the floor by inverting a target acceptance length
options.description: Choosing this picks the tokens-per-window to aim at and derives the floor that implies it, instead of sweeping floors.
options.insight:
- **The field's method:** vLLM's `_acceptance_length_to_rates(length, n)` turns a target mean acceptance length into per-position rates via a minimum-variance schedule.
- **Why it is the right shape:** the objective becomes the metric that matters, and the floor becomes its solution.

options.label: Skip it - more passes on the existing measurement
options.description: Choosing this spends the time tightening the throughput estimate instead of adding a new view.
options.insight:
- **The argument:** the throughput effect is +8-11% and already beats this window's noise floor, so the decision could be taken on what exists.
- **Breaks when:** the next question is *why* the rate fell, which is the question the law's veto turns on.

options.label: Do it as part of the next floor sweep
options.description: Choosing this folds the per-position reading into the sweep that is already planned rather than making it its own round.
options.insight:
- **Why it is efficient:** the sweep already boots once and runs many arms, so the counter adds no boots.
- **Tradeoff:** the sweep's arms differ in floor, so the per-position shape arrives attached to those settings rather than as a baseline.

batch_depth.prompt: Our concurrent path runs entirely draftless - the engine logs `slot drafts accepted 0 of 0` - while vLLM, TensorRT-LLM and MLC-LLM all key draft depth to batch size. What should be done?

options.label: Arm coupled MTP drafting in the slot path
options.description: Choosing this finishes the work item that would let concurrent requests draft, which is currently switched off for correctness reasons.
options.insight:
- **What is known:** `STRATA_BATCH_MTP=0` is deliberate - the launcher records that coupled drafts engage on the serial path but not yet in slots, blocked on counter and cell staging, and to flip it only when that work lands.
- **What the field says is at stake:** three independent engines key speculative depth to batch size, and TensorRT-LLM notes its speedups are "only observable at low batch sizes" - the regime our pair probe measures.
- **Cost:** engine work with a correctness gate, plus MMLU after, because an earlier batch-side rescue bent the distribution and took MMLU from 95.7 to 91.4-92.9.

options.label: Measure the slot path's ceiling first
options.description: Choosing this establishes what draftless concurrency costs before building anything, by comparing it with the serial path at the same content.
options.insight:
- **What we have:** 110.7 and 110.2 t/s pair aggregates at two floors, against about 160 t/s single-stream - so a concurrent request costs roughly a third of a serial one.
- **Why measure first:** the pair path's window cost is 17.39 ms for 2.00 rows, and the same decode-timing line tells us where that goes before any change.

options.label: Add a batch-keyed depth schedule like the field's
options.description: Choosing this sets draft depth per concurrency level, following the schedule pattern three engines ship, once the slot path can draft at all.
options.insight:
- **The field's exact form:** TensorRT-LLM `draft_len_schedule = {100: 4, 200: 3, 300: 2}`; vLLM `num_speculative_tokens_per_batch_size` entries of `(range_start, range_end, tokens)`; MLC-LLM a 4/3/2/0 table.
- **Why it is the natural target here:** our window size is already a per-request value, so a schedule is a policy rather than a new mechanism.
- **Depends on:** the slot path drafting at all, which is item a.

options.label: Leave the slot path alone
options.description: Choosing this accepts draftless concurrency as it is and keeps the effort on the single-stream axis the bar is stated on.
options.insight:
- **Why it is defensible:** the bar is a single-stream number, and concurrency has not regressed - 110.7 versus 110.2 across arms, and 176.5 aggregate at six-concurrent on an earlier boot.
- **What it leaves on the table:** the one lane where three surveyed engines find their speculative wins, and our own aggregate is at 110 where a single stream reads 160.

options.label: Only after the single-stream frontier is settled
options.description: Choosing this sequences the batch work behind the current floor and policy decisions.
options.insight:
- **Why the order:** the slot path's correctness gate needs the same instrumentation (per-position, coupled counters) the single-stream work is about to build.
- **Cost:** the concurrent lane stays at zero drafts for at least one more session.

typical_accept_arm.prompt: Our typical-acceptance rescue is a bare constant, `STRATA_TYPICAL_ACCEPT=0.2`, while Medusa accepts within `min(epsilon, delta * exp(-H(p)))` and Hydra sweeps its threshold over 0.05-0.25. What should be done with ours?

options.label: Sweep the constant first, quality-gated
options.description: Choosing this measures the rescue's threshold at several values with the graded suites in the same window.
options.insight:
- **Why it needs the gate:** this is the one acceptance path in our engine that is deliberately not distribution-matching - Medusa states that scheme treats exact distribution matching as unnecessary, and EAGLE-2/3 exclude it from their temperature-1 tables for that reason.
- **The field's range:** Hydra sweeps epsilon over 0.05-0.25 and plots speculation length against judged generation quality, which is the two-axis form our six-metric law already asks for.
- **Here now:** the standing value 0.2 sits inside that range but has never been swept here.

options.label: Add the entropy term, Medusa's co-threshold
options.description: Choosing this makes the threshold scale with how flat the model's distribution is, so it widens automatically on uncertain text.
options.insight:
- **The mechanism:** accept within `min(epsilon, delta * exp(-H(p)))`, so a flat distribution relaxes the requirement and a sharp one tightens it.
- **Why it fits a variable workload:** our content classes differ enough that tokens/window ranged 2.5-4.0 at one setting, which is what an entropy term is for.
- **Cost:** engine work plus the graded gate, since it changes which tokens are emitted.

options.label: Turn it off and keep only exact verification
options.description: Choosing this removes the partial-acceptance rescue so every emitted token is verified exactly.
options.insight:
- **What it buys:** the invariance argument becomes literally true for our engine, so the graded gate on draft-only changes could be skipped on principle.
- **What it costs:** the rescue exists because it was measured to help; the launcher records a threshold of 0.2 as part of the adopted recipe.
- **Breaks when:** the acceptance rate falls enough that the lost drafts outweigh the exactness gain.

options.label: Leave it at 0.2
options.description: Choosing this changes nothing about the rescue and keeps the effort on the floor and the policy.
options.insight:
- **Why it is reasonable:** it is part of an adopted recipe that was measured net-positive, and no regression has been attributed to it.
- **What stays unknown:** whether 0.2 is near the optimum, since it has never been swept on this machine.

options.label: Measure its quality effect before touching it at all
options.description: Choosing this runs the graded suites on the current setting so any future change has a baseline to be judged against.
options.insight:
- **Why first:** the campaign has been burned by a batch-side acceptance change that took MMLU from 95.7 to 91.4-92.9, and this is the same class of knob.
- **Cost:** one boot and two suites.

spec_prob_arm.prompt: The engine ships two exact-verification acceptance paths that the standing recipe does not use: `STRATA_SPEC_PROB=1` (rejection sampling, lossless by construction) and `STRATA_SPEC_GUMBEL=1` (Gumbel-max coupling, ported from llama.cpp's lab branch). Which should be measured?

options.label: Both, interleaved in one window
options.description: Choosing this A/Bs the two lossless acceptance paths against the standing recipe in a single boot.
options.insight:
- **Why they matter to this decision:** both accept drafts by a rule that provably preserves the target's distribution, so they raise acceptance without the quality question the typical-acceptance rescue carries.
- **What exists:** rejection sampling at src/core/mtp.cpp:580 and src/core/verify.cpp:2313, and Gumbel-max coupling at src/kernels/cuda/sampler.cu:1112.
- **Cost:** the same single-boot interleaved instrument, since neither is a config-file change.

options.label: STRATA_SPEC_PROB only
options.description: Choosing this measures the rejection-sampling path alone, the one with the cleanest lossless guarantee.
options.insight:
- **Why it is the cleaner arm:** Gumbel coupling changes the sampling draw itself, while rejection sampling judges the existing draw against the target's distribution.
- **Here now:** neither is in the standing recipe.

options.label: Gumbel-max coupling only
options.description: Choosing this measures the llama.cpp-lab port alone.
options.insight:
- **Why it is interesting:** it comes from the same lineage as llama.cpp's coupled drafting, which is the project whose floor practice is closest to ours.
- **Cost:** it changes the sampling path, so the graded suites belong in the same window.

options.label: Not now - the floor decision comes first
options.description: Choosing this defers both paths until the current trade is settled.
options.insight:
- **Why the order is defensible:** the floor is a one-line change with a measured effect, while these are engine paths that interact with the sampling code the quality metrics depend on.
- **Cost:** a lossless way to raise acceptance stays unmeasured.

options.label: Only with the graded suites in the same window
options.description: Choosing this makes MMLU-Pro and mimic a precondition for either arm.
options.insight:
- **Why the caution:** both paths sit in the sampler, which is exactly where the earlier batch rescue bent the distribution.
- **Cost:** two suites per arm, on a quiet lane.

autotune_ownership.prompt: Who should set the values the lane runs with - the floor, the split, the depth?

options.label: Hand-tuned config, as today
options.description: Choosing this keeps every value in strata-iq3_s.json, set by measurement and changed deliberately.
options.insight:
- **What it buys:** every value has a dated measurement behind it and a single place to revert.
- **What it costs:** the config cannot follow the content, and two of its values are already stale - the split is pinned while the engine's own refinement sits dormant, and the floor sits above every surveyed project's.

options.label: Run tools/calibrate.py per machine and commit its pick
options.description: Choosing this derives the values from the engine's own live-engine sweep and freezes them into the config.
options.insight:
- **What it is:** the shipped tool sweeps `SPEC_MIN_PS = (0.3, 0.5, 0.7)` and `PCIE_FRACS` over seven values on a running engine and reports the best pair.
- **Why it is better than hand-tuning:** the sweep happens on the machine that will run it, in one boot, with no cross-boot comparison.
- **Breaks when:** the workload changes shape, since the pick is a constant again.

options.label: A runtime policy owns it
options.description: Choosing this lets the engine decide depth and split per request from measured cost, with the config as a starting point.
options.insight:
- **What already exists:** DraftPolicy's expected-tokens-per-millisecond tables, and PcieAuto's refinement of the split from the measured pool rate and link rate - the latter dormant because the config pins the value and because of a batch-path guard.
- **The field's precedent:** SGLang's adaptive controller is the only surveyed closed loop; the others schedule by batch size.
- **Cost:** behaviour becomes harder to reproduce exactly, which the proof law cares about.

options.label: Offline sweep sets the start, the policy adapts from there
options.description: Choosing this uses the calibration tool to choose a starting point and the runtime policy to move within it.
options.insight:
- **Why the combination fits the evidence:** every surveyed engine that adapts also has a documented default, and the sweeps show the optimum moves with hardware and workload.
- **Here now:** both halves exist in this repository and neither is wired to the other.

options.label: Re-enable the engine's own dormant self-tuning first
options.description: Choosing this unblocks PcieAuto - the refinement the config currently prevents - before adding new tuning.
options.insight:
- **What blocks it:** generate.cpp:2829 gates the whole block on `o.pcie_frac < 0.0` and the config passes 0.35 explicitly, so the link has never been probed; and generate.cpp:8353 requires `o.batch == 0` while this lane runs the batch path.
- **What it is worth:** the split itself measured only +-4% in a per-request sweep, so the prize here is the measurement, not the value.
- **Honest reading:** worth doing for the link number, not for a speedup.

lane_exclusivity.prompt: Tonight the engine log held 90 request lines for this boot against the ~29-38 I issued, so a parallel program shared port 8081 for part of it. Should the harness refuse to measure while another client is active?

options.label: Hard refuse - stop and say why
options.description: Choosing this makes every probe check for a foreign request first and abort rather than record a contaminated number.
options.insight:
- **Why it matters:** two rounds of this campaign were voided by a shared lane and one of tonight's candidates had to be re-run for exactly this reason.
- **Cheapest implementation:** the engine log's request lines are the witness - count them across a fixed idle window before and after a probe.
- **Cost:** probes occasionally refuse to run while the operator is using the model, which is the point.

options.label: Warn and stamp the lane state on every number
options.description: Choosing this lets a run proceed but records the lane's occupancy beside every result.
options.insight:
- **Why it is often enough:** interleaved arms stay comparable when the reader knows the lane was shared.
- **Breaks when:** a result is quoted later without its stamp, which is how remembered comparators creep in.

options.label: No - the interleaved design already controls it
options.description: Choosing this keeps the current practice: arms interleaved forward then reversed, so a busy lane adds noise rather than bias.
options.insight:
- **The argument:** tonight's arm effect reproduced causally in tokens/window (2.76-2.96 against 2.24-2.41) even though the absolutes were suspect.
- **Breaks when:** the effect is smaller than the contamination, which is the +-5% band this campaign keeps meeting.

options.label: Add a lane lease file
options.description: Choosing this makes each measurement program claim a lease in the workspace and refuse to start if another holds it.
options.insight:
- **Why a lease rather than a check:** it stops two of my own sessions from starting at all, which is the actual failure mode seen tonight.
- **Cost:** a stale lease after a crash needs an expiry or the lane locks itself out.

options.label: Coordinate quiet windows manually
options.description: Choosing this keeps the protocol as it is and relies on the operator not using the model while a gate runs.
options.insight:
- **Cost:** nothing to build.
- **Breaks when:** a session runs unattended, which is exactly when tonight's contamination happened.

doctrine_amendment.prompt: The standing law's M3 clause is what vetoed the change. Should AGENTS.md be amended, and how?

options.label: Yes - M3 becomes the acceptance length
options.description: Choosing this replaces the rate with tokens per verify window in the law, keeping the rate as a reported diagnostic.
options.insight:
- **Why the wording is the issue:** the veto came from the clause naming a ratio whose denominator moves with the very knob under test.
- **What the amendment must carry:** the old and new definitions, the date, and the field evidence that the rate is a diagnostic rather than an objective.
- **Risk to state:** redefining a metric is the one move that can make a trade disappear, so it is recorded as a metric change, not a win.

options.label: Yes - M3 carries both numbers
options.description: Choosing this keeps the rate and adds the length, requiring both wherever M3 is quoted.
options.insight:
- **Why it is the conservative amendment:** nothing is removed, so no past number loses its meaning, and the pair is what the systems that compute both actually publish.
- **Breaks when:** reports quote one number without the other.

options.label: No - the law stands, and 0.7 stands with it
options.description: Choosing this leaves both the metric and the floor untouched.
options.insight:
- **What it accepts:** that our scoreboard is stricter than every surveyed engine's, and that the measured +8-11% stays unclaimed.
- **Breaks when:** the same trade is re-derived next session and reaches the same veto.

options.label: Add a clause requiring field practice to be cited
options.description: Choosing this amends the proof law so a trade decision must cite comparable engines' published practice alongside its own numbers.
options.insight:
- **Why it would have changed tonight:** the veto was reached without any external evidence, and eighteen comparables moved the reading of the same numbers.
- **Cost:** every future trade decision carries a research step, which is what this push asked for.

options.label: Add an invariance pre-check for draft-only knobs
options.description: Choosing this writes down which knobs cannot change the emitted distribution, so the graded gate is required only where it can.
options.insight:
- **What it would say:** a knob that only chooses which drafts are offered, with every offered draft verified exactly, cannot change the output; a knob that changes the acceptance rule itself (typical acceptance) can.
- **Why it is precise:** it puts the graded suites where they matter - our armed rescue at 0.2 - instead of on every config change.
- **Evidence:** Medusa's scheme is explicitly not distribution-matching, while a probability floor is; that distinction is the whole clause.

next_priority.prompt: Where should the next session's work go first?

options.label: The floor frontier, with the per-position view
options.description: Choosing this finishes the draft-yield question: sweep the floors, read where the chains die, adopt the measured best.
options.insight:
- **What is already known:** 0.5 and 0.35 both win throughput in every interleaved comparison, and tokens/window rises 2.2 to 2.5-2.9.
- **What is missing:** the per-position shape and the graded gate, both of which the instrument can produce in one boot each.

options.label: Policy-driven depth from the engine's own tables
options.description: Choosing this builds the adaptive depth decision, so the chain follows content instead of a constant.
options.insight:
- **Why it is the structural version of this round's finding:** the optimum floor differs by content class, which is why the field's adaptive engines steer depth rather than fix it.
- **What exists:** the EMA cost and token tables, the margin, and a probe rule for unmeasured sizes.

options.label: The miss path and the resident set
options.description: Choosing this attacks the term that dominates a degraded window, where the measured arithmetic already points above the bar.
options.insight:
- **The arithmetic:** at a 97.9% hit rate the real-workload class at tokens/window 3.96 computes to about 264 t/s against 111.7 at the 88.9% it actually ran at.
- **Why it is the biggest single number on the board:** the CPU term is misses times about 85 microseconds each, and the hit rate ranged 79.5-99.2% within one boot.

options.label: The batch path's draftless concurrency
options.description: Choosing this works the one lane where three surveyed engines find their speculative wins and ours drafts nothing.
options.insight:
- **Here now:** the engine logs `slot drafts accepted 0 of 0`, and concurrency aggregates at about 110 t/s where a single stream reads 160.
- **Blocked on:** the coupled-draft counter work the launcher records as the precondition for switching batch MTP on.

options.label: The R17 draft head
options.description: Choosing this raises acceptance itself rather than banking more of the same drafts.
options.insight:
- **Why the field backs it:** FastMTP moved a reused head from 70%/11%/2% to 81%/56%/36% across depths with multi-step training.
- **Where ours stands:** validated at 85.4% stock round-trip, distilled checkpoint at 57.4%, blocked on mixed-KV conditioning.

options.label: Instrumentation and doctrine first
options.description: Choosing this lands the per-position reporting, the lane check and the AGENTS.md amendment before any further optimization.
options.insight:
- **Why it is not busywork:** tonight's decision stalled precisely because the metric could not answer why the rate fell, and because the law's wording encoded the wrong objective.
- **Cost:** one boot plus small edits, and it makes every later session's decisions cheaper.
